description:
REQ-008 and REQ-009 are internally contradictory, making REQ-009's stated purpose ('near-miss-driven bottleneck-knob selection during forced exploration') structurally impossible to achieve with the mechanism REQ-008 mandates. REQ-008's EARS text (behavioral-spec.md:268-275) requires that 'every other aspect of mutate() (base-clamp, step size, post-step clamp, post-rounding clamp, KNOB-COUNT SELECTION) MUST remain byte-identical to the existing implementation' -- i.e. WHICH knob(s) get mutated stays governed by mutate()'s existing uniformly-random pool pick (sol-genome.mjs:166-172, `Math.floor(rng() * remaining.length)` over the full 4-knob KNOB pool), completely independent of `opts.forcedDirection`. `opts.forcedDirection` only overrides a chosen knob's DIRECTION, never WHICH knob gets chosen (REQ-008's edge case explicitly confirms: 'forcedDirection... missing an entry for the CHOSEN knob: falls back to the existing symmetric coin-flip for that knob').

This means when REQ-015's orchestration (behavioral-spec.md:418-419) 'performs a starvation-forced mutation (REQ-008/009)' using `selectBottleneckKnob`'s single identified bottleneck knob (e.g. SOL_GATE_MIN_LIQUIDITY_USD per REQ-009's own worked example, behavioral-spec.md:314-316), mutate()'s independent random knob-count-selection has no obligation to actually select that knob at all. With a 4-knob pool and count in {1,2}, there is a substantial, non-zero probability every starvation-forced pass mutates a knob OTHER than the one selectBottleneckKnob identified as the actual bottleneck -- silently defeating the entire premise of REQ-009 ('WHICH knob gets the forced-loosen this generation is decided by counting which... sub-conditions most often blocked wouldEngage'). No requirement in REQ-008, REQ-009, or REQ-015 specifies a mechanism (e.g. a `forceKnob`/restricted-pool parameter) to guarantee the bottleneck knob is the one actually selected for mutation.

PROP-010 (verification-architecture.md:60) does not catch this: it only asserts that WHATEVER knob mutate() happens to select has the correct DIRECTION when a forcedDirection entry exists for it -- it never asserts the bottleneck knob itself was the one selected. This is a genuine ambiguity/contradiction that Phase 1c must resolve (per dimension 3's Phase-1c bar: 'are the requirements concrete enough to be implemented unambiguously') before Phase 2a, e.g. by adding an explicit knob-restriction parameter to mutate() and updating PROP-010/PROP-012 to assert the bottleneck knob is the one mutated, not merely that its direction is correct when it happens to be chosen.

evidence.snippet: every other aspect of mutate() (base-clamp, step size, post-step clamp, post-rounding clamp, knob-count selection) MUST remain byte-identical to the existing implementation

groundTruthEvidence.snippet: const n = Math.max(1, Math.min(2, count ?? (rng() < 0.5 ? 1 : 2))); ... const idx = Math.floor(rng() * remaining.length) % remaining.length; chosen.push(remaining.splice(idx, 1)[0]);
